changes.text: 这份记述出自《南方》作者欧内斯特·沙克尔顿的第一人称自述，他是这支队伍的队长。经过一段乘船航程后，他和全队困在象岛：粮食有限，有人冻伤，而且象岛上根本不会有人来搜寻他们。口粮按足额只够全队吃五个星期。减量可以撑三个月，或许还能靠海豹和象海豹补一些，但沙克尔顿不敢把信心全押在这上面：海滩上的海兽似乎都走了，冬天近了。燃料主要靠海兽脂肪，存量里有三只海豹和两张半带脂肪的兽皮。初步估量形势后，他决定全队每天只吃一顿热食。

This account comes from the first-person narrative of Ernest Shackleton, author of South and leader of this party. After a boat journey, he and his men were stranded on Elephant Island: food was limited, a man was frostbitten, and there was no chance at all of any search being made for them there. At full ration the food would last the whole party five weeks. Cut back, it could be spread over three months, and would probably be supplemented to some extent by seals and sea-elephants — but Shackleton dared not count on that with full confidence. The animals seemed to have deserted the beach and winter was near. They were mainly dependent on blubber for fuel, and their stocks included three seals and two and a half skins with the blubber attached. After a preliminary survey of the situation, he decided the party must be limited to one hot meal a day.
两位医生麦基尔罗伊（McIlroy）和麦克林（Macklin）都想随行，但明白自己的职责是留在岛上照顾病号。有人提议把双脚冻伤的布莱克博罗（Blackborrow）带上船，让他尽快得到温暖和庇护。队长否掉了这个提议。记录里给的理由是存活推断：健康的人在船上都难活，重病躺在舱底、动弹不得的人，熬不过必定会遇到的坏天气。

The two doctors, McIlroy and Macklin, were both anxious to go but realized that their duty lay on the island with the sick men. One proposal was to take Blackborrow, the man with the frostbitten feet, so that he could have shelter and warmth as quickly as possible. The leader vetoed it. The record gives survival reasoning: fit men would find it hard enough to live in the boat, and a sick man lying helpless in the bottom could not be expected to survive the heavy weather they were sure to encounter.
名单最后定为沃斯利、克林、麦克尼什（McNeish）、麦卡锡（McCarthy）、文森特（Vincent）和队长本人六人。另一件事是加固小船：队长把木匠（他也在这六人之中）叫来，请他想办法让小船更耐风浪；木匠先问自己是不是随行的人，听说「Yes」显得相当高兴。他年过五十，身体不算好。

The list closed at six: Worsley, Crean, McNeish, McCarthy, Vincent, and the leader himself. A separate matter was strengthening the boat: the leader called the carpenter (he was one of the six) and asked whether he could do anything to make the boat more seaworthy; the carpenter's first question was whether he was going along, and hearing "Yes," he seemed quite pleased. He was over fifty and not altogether fit.
把这几个决定放在一起看，一种解释是：真正让这个方案说得出口的，是最坏情形那笔账。出海的人带一个月口粮，失败就是失败，而留下的人在冬天少了几张要吃饭的嘴；最坏情形被算成：也不会给留下的人增加风险。本文推断，当所有选项都糟透时，人们愿意跟从的未必是更有希望的那条路，而可能是把代价算清楚、不把损失转嫁给同伴的那条路。

Read together, these decisions suggest one explanation: what made the plan speakable was the arithmetic of the worst case. The boat party carried a month's provisions; if they failed, they failed. The men left behind would have fewer mouths to feed through the winter. The worst case was calculated as adding nothing to the risks of the men left on the island. This piece infers that when every option is grim, people will follow not necessarily the more hopeful road, but the one that costs its losses honestly and does not shift them onto comrades.
拒绝病号上船那一条，读起来最不舒服，但记录里给的是存活推断，不是道德立场：健康的人在船上都难活，重病躺舱底的人熬不过坏天气。本文推断，这种取舍的难处不在决定本身，而在它必须给出理由——有人提了建议，被否掉了，记述里写明了否决的理由。原文没有说这些理由是否当众向全队讲过；若是讲过，代价至少由全队一起看见，而不是由某个被悄悄放下的人独自承担，但这只是未经证实的推测。

The refusal of the sick man is the least comfortable paragraph to read, yet the record offers survival reasoning rather than a moral stance: fit men would find it hard enough to live in the boat, and a sick man lying helpless in the bottom would not survive the heavy weather. This piece infers that the difficulty of such a trade-off lies less in the decision itself than in having to give reasons for it: a proposal was made and vetoed, and the account sets down why. The original does not say whether those reasons were put to the whole party; if they were, the cost would at least have been visible to everyone rather than borne by one person quietly set aside — but that is an unverified conjecture.
还有一处值得留意：记述说他决定征求志愿者，同时心里早有人选。本文提出的一种替代做法是直接点名，省掉征求的形式；但若按记述的叙述顺序读——先写这件事需要向全队详细论证危险和理由，再写决定征求志愿者，最后落名单——这种安排可能让名单更像共识而不是指派。原文没有写明当众论证与征求志愿的实际先后，也没有写明是否确已征求；这只是一种解释，原文也没有说明他为什么这样安排。

One more detail catches the eye: the account says he decided to call for volunteers while already knowing his choices. One alternative this piece raises would have been simply to name names and skip the formality. But if one reads by the order of the narrative — first that the case had to be argued to the party in some detail, then the decision to call for volunteers, then the settled list — the arrangement may make the list read as consensus rather than assignment. The original does not state the actual order of the arguing and the call for volunteers, nor whether volunteers were in fact called for; this is only one reading, and the original gives no reason for the arrangement.
本文提出的一种替代：不派人出去，全员接零活维持现金流。好处是短期内不分散人力，代价是没有人去打开外部通道，四个月后仍然没有援手。

One alternative this piece raises: send nobody out, and have everyone take contract work to keep cash flowing. The gain is that no one is pulled off the front line in the short term; the cost is that no one opens an outside channel, and after four months there is still no help.
